rationale: Algebraically the expression reduces to (ebitda × sale)/(3yr-capx × mktcap), so it is dominated by the 1/capx term and will be driven by near-zero-capex, asset-light firms (a sector/low-investment tilt already spanned by CMA) rather than by any genuine "capex payoff" mechanism, and a single 1% winsorization will not tame a ratio with a small, occasionally-zero denominator.

This is the third instance of the archive's MIN(IND_RANK(oancf/mktcap), IND_RANK(efficiency-improvement)) template (HarvestingCashFlowValue, CheapPredictableCapexYield), with only the second leg swapped, and it does nothing to address the diagnosed problem that the cash-flow-yield leg keeps producing positive FMB slopes alongside negative FF5 alphas.

The second leg is the exact sign-flipped construct already tested in CheapOrganicSalesNoAcquisition (aqc3/at vs. revenue growth), so this is largely a mirror-image rediscovery, and because a ~0–0.2 acquisition-to-assets ratio is differenced against a 3-year growth rate with far larger dispersion, the leg is in practice mostly negative revenue growth rather than M&A capital productivity.

The cash-deficit leg, (capx − oancf)/sale, is a genuinely different construct from the capex-trend and capex-volatility legs already tested and interacts coherently with the sales multiple, with the expected negative sign matching the expression's direction; the main caveat is substantial overlap with the documented external-financing/negative-FCF anomaly, which the test should control for.

This is a continuous restatement of the already-tested EbitdaValueMarginalPPEPayoff / PriceyCapitalProductivityFade family (value × growth-minus-capacity-growth gap) with sale substituted for ebitda, and the division by mktcap/sale makes magnitude explode for the cheapest firms so the ranking is dominated by the value leg rather than the operating-leverage idea.

Structurally identical to the archived PriceyCapitalProductivityFade — same MUL(IND_RANK(mktcap/sale), IND_RANK(NEG(TREND(productivity)))) template with only the productivity numerator/denominator and window changed — and the emp-based denominator is coarse and stale enough that a 3-point trend in oancf/emp is mostly noise.
